subject: Failover liability heatmap & proposed RTO/RPO allocations for multi-region setup
messages:
From: Chris Park <chris.park@bigbank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@bigbank.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarification: failover liability allocation + RTO/RPO expectations

Jordan,

Thanks for the productive demo last week. As we prepare procurement + legal review, we need a clearer statement of how Redwood expects to allocate liability and credits in a multi-region failover scenario. Our internal risk group put together a short heatmap showing regions by impact and desired RTO/RPO; attaching here (see redwood-ask-heatmap.png).

Top asks from our side:
- Explicit RTO/RPO per region and per failure class (region outage vs whole-cloud outage)
- When Redwood will accept service credits vs when third-party cloud/network vendors will be the responsible party
- Any standby activation windows (lead time) that would change liabilities
- Exceptions for planned maintenance and force majeure

We prefer a single page mapping so our legal team can compare to other vendors. Can you propose concrete contract language or a heatmap that maps obligations, credit triggers, and liability caps? Also flag any implementation constraints (warm-standby availability, data residency impacts, etc.).

Appreciate a response by EOD Wednesday so we can keep the procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Chris Park
Head of Cloud Risk
BigBank Inc.

Attachment: bigbank-risk-heatmap-20270621.png (image/png)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Chris Park <chris.park@bigbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarification: failover liability allocation + RTO/RPO expectations

Chris — thanks for the heatmap and the clear asks. Attaching a first-draft "Redwood failover liability heatmap" (redwood-failover-heatmap-v1.png) and a short narrative below. High level summary up front:

- We propose tiered obligations by failure class: local-region outage, regional-network partition, and full-cloud event. Each class has different RTO targets and credit triggers.
- For local-region outages (single-AZ or single-region hardware faults): Redwood stands behind 99.95% availability per region; failover to a warm standby (if enabled) is considered an operational action and has a defined activation window we can agree to.
- For regional-network partitions or multi-region events: we propose contiguous RTO windows (warm-standby activation 1–4 hours depending on configuration) and differentiated credit bands.
- We highlight carveouts: third-party interconnect failures (cloud provider network down), data residency/legal holds, and scheduled maintenance.

Proposed next steps:
1) Karthik / Hannah to review and confirm technical feasibility for the 1–4 hour standby windows we map in the heatmap.
2) If agreed, Redwood legal will produce redlines to the SLA. I attached a lightweight template language in the Drive link and will follow up with a DocuSign link once legal has reviewed.
3) Schedule an executive call if liability caps need to be escalated.

I've CC'd Karthik/Hannah for the technical confirmation. If anything in the heatmap looks off, flag it in a reply-all.

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-failover-heatmap-v1.png (image/png)
Related: https://drive.google.com/open?id=abc123
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Chris Park <chris.park@bigbank.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: failover liability allocation + RTO/RPO expectations

Chris — adding a technical viewpoint to Jordan's commercial framing. I reviewed your heatmap and Jordan's draft. A few concrete notes so the legal language maps cleanly to what we can deliver: 

1) Definitions: we need to be explicit about "activation window" vs "time-to-restore". Activation window = how long we take to initiate failover to a standby (purpose-built), time-to-restore = time until user traffic is served at target latency SLOs. Those are often conflated.

2) Proposed concrete targets (config-dependent):
   - Local-region hardware fault: activation < 15 minutes (auto-recover where possible), time-to-restore to SLOs typically < 30 minutes for stateless workloads; RPO = 0 (KV/prefix caching) for non-persistent paths.
   - Regional warm-standby (pre-provisioned but not active): activation window 1–4 hours (we recommend 2 hours standard), RPO = 15 minutes for stateful components if you enable cross-region replicated KV/caching.
   - Cold-standby or rebuild from snapshot: activation window 6–24 hours, RPO = snapshot granularity (hourly/daily).

3) Cloud provider network carveout: if the underlying cloud region is unavailable due to provider network issues (BGP/interconnect), Redwood will use fallbacks where possible, but the SLA will include a provider carveout for inability to move traffic across provider backbone. We can add a subclause that binds Redwood to reasonable efforts to mitigate via alternate regions and CDN edge routing, with documentation of those efforts.

4) Liability mapping suggestion: tie credit bands to time-to-restore to SLOs rather than activation window alone. Activation window can vary by customer config; credits should be for measurable customer impact (e.g., failed API requests above X% over an hour).

I'll attach a redline of the SLA language with the specific RTO/RPO bands and the recommended cap math (see attached proposed-sla-redlines.docx). Happy to walk legal through the technical assumptions.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed-sla-redlines.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)
From: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@bigbank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Chris Park <chris.park@bigbank.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 17:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: failover liability allocation + RTO/RPO expectations

Jordan / Karthik — thanks for the quick turn. The heatmap and the redlines look promising. A few follow-ups from legal: 

- We need explicit language for the EU region regarding data residency and a guaranteed RPO no worse than 15 minutes for stateful workloads that are in-scope of GDPR controls. Can Redwood commit to that in the redline? If not, we need clear exceptions mapped out.
- For multi-region events where traffic must be shifted cross-continental, we want a running log of mitigation steps that Redwood took (timestamped) so our auditors can reconstruct timelines. Please confirm Redwood will provide a post-incident timeline as part of the SLA incident report.
- Liability cap: BigBank prefers a pro-rata daily service credit tied to time-to-restore to SLOs as Karthik suggested. We will propose specific percentages in our redlines, but please share any constraints on your side.

Let's schedule a 30-minute call Friday to align on the EU RPO ask and to confirm whether our preferred 2-hour activation window (for EU warm-standby) is technically feasible without additional reserved capacity. Jordan — can you propose two slots?

Thanks,
Lisa Gomez (on behalf of BigBank legal)
BigBank Inc.
